`countsynth` is a full port of the Python package `bayesian_panel_nmf`
(NumPyro/JAX): same model, same priors, same estimands, same artifact
layout. This vignette maps the two.

## Config mapping

`read_countsynth_config()` accepts Python YAML configs verbatim. Renamed keys
(everything else keeps its name and default):

| Python YAML | R / cmdstanr |
|---|---|
| `mcmc.num_warmup` | `iter_warmup` |
| `mcmc.num_samples` | `iter_sampling` |
| `mcmc.thinning` | `thin` |
| `mcmc.target_accept` | `adapt_delta` |
| `mcmc.random_seed` | `seed` |
| `mcmc.num_chains` / `chain_method` | `chains` / `parallel_chains` (`"vectorized"` warns and runs parallel) |
| `output.save_traces` (NetCDF) | posterior draws saved as RDS |

Thinning semantics are identical: both run `num_samples` post-warmup
iterations and retain `num_samples / thinning`.

## Command equivalents

| Python CLI | R |
|---|---|
| `countsynth run --config cfg.yaml` | `countsynth_run("cfg.yaml")` |
| `countsynth run --type total --rank 5` | `countsynth_run(cfg, types = "total", ranks = 5)` |
| `countsynth viz --results ...` | `countsynth_report(draws, output_dir)` |
| `countsynth viz --tables-only` | `countsynth_report(draws, dir, figures = character())` |
| `countsynth traces file.nc` | `parameter_diagnostics(fit)` / `countsynth_trace_plot(fit)` |

## Draws artifact

The tidy draws frame has the same schema in both languages: 1-indexed
`.draw` / `.chain` / `.iteration`, then `unit`, `time`, `group`, `outcome`,
`denominator`, `treatment`, `ypred`, `mu`, `mu_treated`. As in Python, `mu`
is the **untreated** log-count surface and `mu_treated = mu + te`; `ypred`
is the counterfactual (untreated) posterior predictive. Cut runs add
`cut_component`, `stage1_draw`, `stage1_chain`, `stage1_iteration`.

## What is checked, and what is not

- **Checked — exact:** the Stan models' log-densities equal the NumPyro
  models' at shared parameter values, up to an additive constant (fixtures
  exported from Python; run `testthat::test_file("test-logdensity-parity.R")`).
  Cell flattening order, cut chain quotas, output-thinning strides, and gate
  bands are also fixture-pinned.
- **Checked — statistical:** posterior summaries on the bundled fertility
  data agree within Monte Carlo error.
- **Not preserved:** bitwise draw identity. NUTS implementations and RNGs
  differ; the cut components selected for the same seed also differ (R and
  numpy RNGs are different streams with the same stratified logic).

## Implementation differences worth knowing

- Stan's `joint.stan` doubles as the cut stage-1 model via the
  `model_treated` data flag; Python keeps two deliberately duplicated model
  files pinned together by a parity test.
- The counterfactual `ypred` RNG clamps the log-mean at ~20.79
  (`exp(x) < 2^30`) because Stan's count RNGs overflow above that; NumPyro
  returns huge float draws instead. Irrelevant at realistic count scales.
- `countsynth` reports rely on the identical estimand formulas
  (`sum(exp(mu))`-based excess, person-year-weighted rates, two-sided
  posterior p-values), reproduced from `tables.py` / `plots.py`.
